label: GO, choosing a1 after an unrewarded trial that did not end in S1, early in the episode
explanation: Fires only at GO (100% of mass), never at D1 or D2. It fires only when the previous trial was unrewarded (prev_reward 0, 100% of mass) and the agent is choosing a1 (model_act/action a1, 99.9% of mass; the policy logit for a1 is strongly positive, 72% of mass in the top choice bin). The previous trial reached S2, or is outside the window (prev_state -1). So the unit encodes an a1 choice after S2 went unrewarded, which is consistent with both a model-based stay after rare-unrewarded a1 and a switch to a1 after common-unrewarded a2. It also needs the episode to be early: it is silent from ep_trial ~45 onward (0 activations in trials 50-99) and strongest in trials 3-30. Value is in a narrow band (7.73-8.10). Does not fire after rewarded trials, when choosing a2, or after an unrewarded S1 outcome. Dev results: (GO & prev_reward 0 & a1) gives recall 0.99 but precision 0.19; adding ep_trial<40 gives F1 0.65; adding prev_state != 1 gives F1 0.785 with mass recall 0.99. Adding a choice-logit threshold reaches 0.80, but I left it out for simplicity. Top activations usually come after two or more unrewarded trials in a row in which a1 was chosen. Precision is limited (~0.66) because many matching early GO steps stay silent, so I call it partially explained. The predicate uses only observed history plus the agent's own upcoming choice.
